name: E-book Reader
description: Read 18 e-book formats — EPUB, PDF, TXT, MOBI, AZW3, DOCX, comics and more — with paged, double-page or scrolling layouts, text-to-speech, translation, highlights and notes. Books and notes are written to a real folder on your disk through a bundled native sidecar.

versions.releaseNotes: 18 book formats, paged/double-page/scrolling layouts, text-to-speech, translation, highlights and notes, real on-disk library via native sidecar, in-app folder picker. v1.2.2: visible previous/next page buttons in every paged layout, working double-page spread, swipe-to-turn on touch screens, and imported PDFs now keep the file name on disk instead of the stale embedded title. v1.2.3: PDFs whose embedded fonts cannot be mapped are detected automatically and re-rendered with system fonts, so Chinese text is readable instead of showing the wrong characters. v1.2.4: paged layouts no longer push the paper off-screen — text now paginates inside a fixed page while the sheet stays put, so single and double page both show complete, readable pages for TXT and every other text format; double page actually splits the screen in two; code and command lines are no longer stretched by justification; the page adds proper inner margins. v1.2.5: Chinese PDFs whose embedded fonts cannot be mapped now recover both the page text and the document metadata (title/author) instead of showing mojibake; detection samples several pages so files with a clean cover no longer slip through. Translation and WebDAV backup now go through the bundled native sidecar, because the host sandbox blocks page-level fetch — so any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or self-hosted WebDAV server works, not just a hard-coded allow-list. The folder picker gains a real address bar (paste D://Books and press Enter), an "open in file manager" button, and a narrow-panel layout that no longer truncates folder names to a single character. The .dbxp now ships LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and every third-party licence text, and all book HTML is sanitised by one strict allow-list before it is mounted.

18 book formats, paged/double-page/scrolling layouts, text-to-speech, translation, highlights and notes, real on-disk library via native sidecar, in-app folder picker. v1.2.2: visible previous/next page buttons in every paged layout, working double-page spread, swipe-to-turn on touch screens, and imported PDFs now keep the file name on disk instead of the stale embedded title. v1.2.3: PDFs whose embedded fonts cannot be mapped are detected automatically and re-rendered with system fonts, so Chinese text is readable instead of showing the wrong characters. v1.2.4: paged layouts no longer push the paper off-screen — text now paginates inside a fixed page while the sheet stays put, so single and double page both show complete, readable pages for TXT and every other text format; double page actually splits the screen in two; code and command lines are no longer stretched by justification; the page adds proper inner margins. v1.2.5: Chinese PDFs whose embedded fonts cannot be mapped now recover both the page text and the document metadata (title/author) instead of showing mojibake; detection samples several pages so files with a clean cover no longer slip through. Translation and WebDAV backup now go through the bundled native sidecar, because the host sandbox blocks page-level fetch — so any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or self-hosted WebDAV server works, not just a hard-coded allow-list. The folder picker gains a real address bar (paste D://Books and press Enter), an "open in file manager" button, and a narrow-panel layout that no longer truncates folder names to a single character. The .dbxp now ships LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and every third-party licence text, and all book HTML is sanitised by one strict allow-list before it is mounted. v1.2.6: selecting text in a PDF now works. The PDF text layer *is* the book container, so the old lookup (which searched for a child with that class) always came back empty: the selection toolbar never appeared, and neither highlights nor notes could be added to any PDF. Highlights also get their own style sheet for the transparent text layer, so the colour is actually visible over the rendered page, and saved highlights are redrawn when the document is reopened. v1.2.7: EPUB, TXT, FB2 and RTF get the same treatment. Their text lives in a Shadow DOM tree, and Chrome reports a selection made inside one as collapsed onto the host element, so the toolbar stayed hidden there as well. The reader now asks the shadow root for the real selection and takes the toolbar position from that same range, so selecting text works in every format.
